content.text: I've completed the read-only inspection. Here is the governing review.

input.summary:
Scope of inspection: `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0-design-00a860ab/design.md` (complete), its `audit.md` and two-entry `manifest.sha256`, plan sections D.110c-0c1f5a / f5b0 / f5b (`docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:98036-98654`), and the named current source seams: `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts`, `creator-author-issuance-frontiers.ts`, `latched-acl.ts`, `registry/registry-v1.json`; `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts`, `v3-live.ts`, `internal/creator-transition-advance.ts`, `internal/creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts`, `internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts`; `packages/compaction/src/blueprint-fold.ts`; `packages/issuance-store/src/types.ts` and `maintenance.ts` with `packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts`; and `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts` around `drainRebaseOutbox()`/`issueOwned()` and the public application/session contracts. Honest limitation: this session has no shell, so I read the diff's product of `00a860ab..fc4b8fc7` (the frozen design, its audit, and the amended plan section) directly from the worktree and could not independently recompute the `a5dbd4f4…` manifest SHA-256 or the eight recorded source hashes; all findings below rest on directly read source, not on the audit's asserted digests.

Much of the construction is genuinely well matched to the current product. The transport choice is coherent: `registry/registry-v1.json` declares `kinds.vertex.fields.operation` as an unconstrained `canonical-object` signed under `ts-drp/vertex/v3`, and pins `authorSequence.constraints.reset = "never"`, which the design preserves — so a reserved operation inside the ordinary signed vertex needs no wire field, no second signature, no new suite and no dependency. The old/downgraded-peer barrier really does fail closed: `internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:398` requires exactly one `drp-creator-author-issuance-frontiers-state` in the proposed closure, so an old binary rejects a settlement-mode successor with `TRUST_CLOSURE_INVALID` rather than continuing. The ≤64 frontier vector fits: `latched-acl.ts:134` caps ACL members at 64 and `:148` already enforces strict code-unit author ordering, so "every successor ACL member, not only writers" is representable within the existing `copiedFrontiers` bound. `historyRoot`/`historySize` are available before the checkpoint is prepared (`creator-close.ts:874-882` precedes `:950`), so binding them is implementable. `V3LocalIssueResult` (`v3-live.ts:506`) already carries `{authorSequence, digest}`, and `V3RoomApplication` / `CreateV3RoomSessionInput` (`examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:351,377`) accommodate `hasDisplacedOperation` and `authorSettlementVersion?: 1` as a minimal public boundary. f5a's per-author close-liveness result is not reopened.

The construction nevertheless cannot be authorized as written. Two defects are P0. First, the central admission rule — "enters the causality index, close set, history … but never blueprint admission/reduction" — is unimplementable from the named seams and aborts every close either way: `captureCloseGraph()` (`v3-live.ts:7430-7457`) hard-requires `applicationVertices.size === applicationAuthors.size + 1 === applicationCharges.size + 1 === index.size`, the close set and RFC 9162 history are derived from exactly that map (`creator-close.ts:874-882`), and the same map is handed to `foldBlueprintEpoch` (`v3-live.ts:7039-7051`), which applies **every** vertex through `applyPreparedBlueprintOperation` with no skip and demands `authorize(...) === true` under write authorization (`packages/compaction/src/blueprint-fold.ts:208-228`). Excluding the control vertex breaks the capture invariant and removes the very graph slot the checkpoint scan depends on; including it makes the reducer reject the reserved action. `@ts-drp/compaction` is named in none of the four slices. Second, the author-baseline does not preserve never-resetting issuance: because a fully removed key is *omitted* from the vector, the creator retains no authenticated prior boundary for it, and the baseline is accepted for any author "absent from the prior authenticated checkpoint" with `retireThrough === null` when `lineageNext === 0` — so a removed-and-readmitted same key can restart at sequence 0 and obtain a fresh creator-certified `settledThrough` over slots already signed under different digests. That is precisely the compact unproved maximum (and reset) the design says it prohibits, and the enforcement it relies on lives only in the settling author's own store.

Five further P1s follow the same pattern of promised outcomes without a named owner: settled rows cannot actually leave custody (`closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:404-428` and `browser-issuance-store.ts:651-658` both refuse any prefix whose rows are not all `epoch === closedEpoch` and `published`, so one surviving old-epoch displaced row freezes the watermark forever, and once unpruned covered rows exceed `maxEpochVertices` the room hard-fails at `v3-live.ts:4419`); every vertex-authentication path threads `preparedBlueprintAdmission` (six Node call sites), so the first control row that survives into a later outbox makes `readRebaseOutbox()` return `record-rejected` and the room throw; `ReplacementRef` carries no batch entry index while the room routinely batches up to 16 replacements into one vertex (`examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2654-2681`), so the creator cannot verify the "exact ordered replacement identities" the statement claims to bind; the creator's own author cannot be settled at all because `deriveCreatorIssuanceRetirementBoundary` hard-throws on exactly the displaced-row shape (`creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts:112-127`) and the unmentioned `drp-creator-issuance-retirement-state` record is still cross-checked against the frontier (`creator-transition-advance.ts:418-423`); and seeding the settled prefix from a v1 admitted prefix silently converts today's shipped D.110c-0c1d behavior — pending `covered-historical` rows are reissued at the current epoch — into terminal drop, without an author statement and without a matrix row.

Because at least P0-2 (baseline statement/vector shape) and P1-5 (`ReplacementRef` grammar) change the exact canonical shapes f5b0a RED is meant to freeze, and P0-1/P1-4 change what "the reserved carrier is accepted as" across protocol-v3 and Node, the f5b0a protocol-codec/compatibility RED may not begin as sliced. Amend the design per the required actions, then re-review. Do not implement a nearby substitute. Nothing here authorizes production GREEN or a retained campaign, and f5a's foreign-anomaly result is untouched.

findings.title: Reserved control vertex cannot be in the close graph without entering the blueprint reducer; either branch aborts every close
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:7430-7457` — `captureCloseGraph()` returns `undefined` unless `applicationVertices.size === applicationAuthors.size + 1 === applicationCharges.size + 1 === registration.index.size`. `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:874-882` derives the close-set root, history root and history size from exactly `graph.vertices` / `graph.charges` / `graph.frontier`, and `:487-498` builds the per-author slot map from `graph.authors`. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:7039-7051` hands `copyApplicationVertices(registration.applicationVertices)` to `foldBlueprintEpoch` with `authorize` = `isV3ApplicationAuthorAuthorized` (`:3449-3455`, i.e. `authorizeLatchedApplicationWrite`, permissionless-or-writer). `packages/compaction/src/blueprint-fold.ts:208-228` iterates every vertex in that map, filtering only the anchor hash, throws `BLUEPRINT_AUTHORIZATION_REJECTED` unless `authorize(...) === true`, and calls `stagedMachine.apply(vertex.operation)` → `applyPreparedBlueprintOperation`, which raises `BLUEPRINT_OPERATION_INVALID` for an unregistered action. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3956-3961` shows `retainApplicationVertex` is called immediately after `index.append`, so the two maps are populated together today. Design §"Admission and durable lifecycle" requires both "appends the vertex to the ordinary causality index" / "appears in the close set and RFC 9162 history" and "does not call blueprint operation admission … reducer", and design §"TDD implementation slices" names only protocol-v3, Node, the room and the creator — `@ts-drp/compaction` is named in no slice.
findings.impact: Neither branch is viable. If the control vertex is appended to the causality index but not retained in `applicationVertices`, `captureCloseGraph()` returns `undefined` and `creator-close.ts:847` throws `creator close graph capture failed`, aborting the close; the vertex is also absent from the close set, the history commitment and `graph.authors`, so the design's own rule that "a control vertex's own author sequence is an ordinary graph slot" is false and the checkpoint scan cannot account it. If it is retained, `foldBlueprintEpoch` reduces it, `stageBlueprintEpoch()` returns `fold-rejected`, `stageSnapshot()` fails and `creator-close.ts:841` throws `creator snapshot export failed: not-active` — again aborting the whole close. Separately, the design gates admission on "current ACL envelope membership" (`authorizeLatchedEnvelopeAuthor`, membership only) while the fold predicate requires write authorization, so a member holding only `admin` or `finality` could author one control vertex and permanently abort every close in the room — a room-wide liveness loss from a single authorized non-writer.
findings.required_action: Amend the design to name `@ts-drp/compaction` (`foldBlueprintEpoch`) and `v3-live.ts`'s `captureCloseGraph` / `retainApplicationVertex` accounting as explicit owners, and state the exact rule that excludes reserved control operations from reduction while retaining graph, charge, frontier, close-set and history membership — including the revised capture invariants. State the exact admission authority for the control body (envelope membership vs. application write authorization) and make the fold predicate and the admission predicate provably consistent, so no authorized member can abort a close. Assign the compaction owner to a numbered slice (extend f5b0b or open a new one); it is currently unowned.

findings.title: Author-baseline permits same-key sequence reset after ACL removal, becoming the compact unproved maximum the design forbids
findings.evidence: Design §"Exact carrier grammar": a baseline is "accepted only for an author absent from the prior authenticated checkpoint, during its first authorized epoch, when the outer control vertex author sequence equals `lineageNext`, and only when `retireThrough === null` iff `lineageNext === 0`". Design §"Creator checkpoint and advancement": "A fully removed key is omitted and may return only through the author-baseline rule above." `packages/protocol-v3/src/latched-acl.ts:3` — `AUTHOR = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/`, i.e. the ACL author *is* the raw Ed25519 public key, so "a fresh author key" means a different ACL member. `packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-author-issuance-frontiers.ts:164-185` bounds the vector at 64 entries; `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:511` iterates only `successorAuthors`, so an omitted author's boundary is unrecoverable from the checkpoint chain. The only stated enforcement is prose: "Same-key membership re-entry therefore requires the original monotonic issuance store; loss of that store fails closed and requires a fresh author key."
findings.impact: An author whose durable issuance store is lost (or who chooses to) can be removed from the ACL and re-added by any admin, then issue a baseline with `lineageNext = 0` and `retireThrough = null`. The creator's stated checks — absence from the prior checkpoint, outer sequence equals `lineageNext`, `retireThrough` arithmetic — all pass, and it certifies a fresh `settledThrough` over sequences `0..k` that already exist under different vertex digests in earlier signed checkpoints and archived history. This is exactly the sequence reset/reuse the registry pins as `reset: "never"` and the design says it prohibits, and it is precisely a compact unproved maximum. It also defeats the design's claim that "exact source uniqueness prevents replay, substitution, equivocation": that uniqueness is scoped to a single close graph, so cross-checkpoint slot reuse is never detected. There is no creator-side fact that distinguishes an honest preserved-lineage baseline from a fabricated one.
findings.required_action: Choose and state one enforceable rule: (a) retain removed members' boundaries as authenticated tombstones in the checkpoint and reconcile the resulting growth with the ≤64 vector bound explicitly; or (b) require the baseline to name the exact prior authenticated checkpoint digest and that author's boundary in it, and have the creator verify `lineageNext > priorSettledThrough` against an authenticated predecessor chain; or (c) restrict baselines to authors that have never appeared in any authenticated predecessor checkpoint, and state the exact fail-closed behavior for a returning key. Whichever is chosen changes the baseline statement shape and/or the checkpoint vector, so it must be settled before f5b0a RED freezes canonical shapes.

findings.title: Settled rows cannot leave active custody; state grows with epoch count and hard-fails the rebase outbox reader
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:404-428` — `copiedIssuance` requires a dense prefix beginning at `prunedThroughAuthorSequence + 1`, with every row satisfying `Number(candidate.epoch) === closedEpoch`, `issued === true`, `outbox === true` and `publishState === "published"`; any deviation returns `D109A_OUTBOX_INCOMPLETE`. `packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts:651-658` — `prunePublishedPrefix` throws `invalid("selected issuance row belongs to another epoch")` when `decoded.epoch !== captured.closedEpoch` and `ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED` when any row is still `pending`. `packages/issuance-store/src/types.ts:83-90` — `DurableIssuanceStore` exposes no delete; pruning is the only reclamation. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4349-4355` and `:6418-6425` — `countHistoricalIssuanceRow` caps historical rows at `maxEpochVertices` and `readRebaseOutbox` returns `record-rejected` ("v3 rebase historical plane is at capacity") past that bound; `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2801` turns that into a thrown room failure. Design §"Recovery semantics and pruning" asserts "Existing closed-epoch cleanup may prune them only after durable checkpoint staging, verified successor adoption, rollback-generation retention and availability conditions" and "No state grows with epoch count or number of completed rebases"; neither `closed-epoch-cleanup.ts` nor the issuance-store pruning contract (which has a conformance suite at `packages/issuance-store/src/conformance.ts`) is named as an owner in any slice.
findings.impact: A displaced source row from epoch k that survives above the prune watermark — the exact state settlement exists to create — makes every later single-epoch cleanup refuse with `D109A_OUTBOX_INCOMPLETE`, so the watermark freezes permanently and the outbox grows with every subsequently issued row, i.e. with epoch count. This is not a soft bound: once the unpruned rows at or below the covered/settled boundary exceed `maxEpochVertices`, `readRebaseOutbox()` fails and the room session becomes terminal. The design's age-independence claim is therefore both unmet and load-bearing, and the mechanism that would reclaim the rows refuses the mixed-epoch prefix by construction.
findings.required_action: Name `packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts` and the `@ts-drp/issuance-store` pruning contract with its browser implementation as explicit owners in a numbered slice. State the exact prune rule for a settled prefix that spans epochs — whether `prunePublishedPrefix`'s single-`closedEpoch` and published-only preconditions change, whether multiple per-epoch calls are used, and whether this is a durable-store contract and conformance-vector change (the plan's f5b0 obligation 10 requires this to be frozen, not deferred). If settled old-epoch rows are instead retained, state the exact bound and reconcile it with the `maxEpochVertices` historical cap that hard-fails `readRebaseOutbox()`.

findings.title: Every recovery, rebase and local-issue authentication path rejects a control vertex; the design names only Node ingress
findings.evidence: `preparedBlueprintAdmission` is threaded through six Node authentication sites — `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:2019`, `:2336`, `:3806` (ingress via `extractAuthorizedV3Vertex`), `:4699` (pinned-genesis outbox row), `:4770` (`authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow`, lines 4733-4790) and `:5977` — plus the local issuer gate in `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:3413-3415`, where `operationSchemaForPreparedAdmission` (`:2708-2726`) returns `undefined` for any discriminator absent from the blueprint's registered operations. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6400-6416` turns an unclassifiable outbox row into `record-rejected` ("v3 rebase outbox record is invalid"), and `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2800-2805` throws on that result. Design §"Admission and durable lifecycle" describes only "Node admission authenticates the normal vertex first … then appends the vertex to the ordinary causality index", and design §"TDD implementation slices" assigns "the reserved admission path" solely to f5b0b while confining f5b0a GREEN to "protocol-v3 registry/codecs/exports and conformance".
findings.impact: The first settlement control vertex that survives into a later epoch's issuance outbox cannot be classified by `classifyRebaseRow`/`authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow`, so `readRebaseOutbox()` returns `record-rejected` and the room throws `v3 room rebase outbox failed: record-rejected`, making the session terminal. The design's own rule that "an older settlement-control row is never handed to the application" and is "covered by a later `settlement-control` source entry" therefore has no reachable implementation, and the crash-matrix row "control journaled but unpublished → restart republishes it" is not satisfiable. Local issue of the control vertex is likewise rejected by protocol-v3 before Node is reached.
findings.required_action: Enumerate in the design every `preparedBlueprintAdmission` call site that must recognize the reserved action — ingress, pinned-genesis and covered-historical outbox classification, displaced/recovery authentication, and the protocol-v3 admission-bound transactional issuer — and assign each to a named slice with its exact accept/skip rule. State explicitly how `rebaseIntents` treats a control row and how a terminal (at/below prefix) control row is skipped without failing the scan.

findings.title: ReplacementRef cannot identify a replacement operation inside a batched vertex, so the creator cannot verify the exact ordered replacements the statement claims to bind
findings.evidence: Design §"Exact carrier grammar": `ReplacementRef = { operationDigest; vertex: [epoch, anchorDigest, authorSequence, vertexDigest] }` — no operation index — while the source side does carry `operationIndex` and `operationCount` in `IntentDisposition`. The design gives one formula, `operationDigest = hashDomain("ts-drp/author-settlement-operation/v1", encodeCanonical(operation))`, without saying whether `operation` is the individual application operation or the vertex's whole operation, and requires the creator to verify each ref against "its canonical inner operation digest". `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2654-2681` — `drainSnapshot` groups up to 16 batchable operations of the same `group` into a single `issueOwned` → `issueLocal` call, and `:2950-2962` shows rebase/transform replacements are pushed onto exactly that `pendingIssues` path with `group = action\0policy`. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5844-5865` confirms the resulting vertex carries the single `applicationBatch` action wrapping `batch.entries`.
findings.impact: On the room's normal replacement path a single vertex carries several distinct replacement operations. If `operationDigest` is taken over the vertex operation it is one value shared by up to 16 entries and identifies nothing; if it is taken over an individual entry the creator cannot locate that entry, since the ref carries no index. Either way the creator's verification collapses to "some same-author ancestor vertex with this digest exists", and the design's central claim that the signed statement "binds … exact ordered current replacements" — the basis for its substitution and reordering resistance in review question 2 — is not delivered by the grammar.
findings.required_action: Either add an explicit batch entry index (and the containing operation count) to `ReplacementRef` and state the exact digest preimage for each, or forbid batching for replacement issues and state the room-side rule that guarantees one replacement operation per vertex. State which, and disambiguate the single `operationDigest` formula into the source-intent case and the replacement case. This changes a canonical shape f5b0a RED is meant to freeze.

findings.title: The creator's own author cannot be settled, and the unmentioned creator-issuance-retirement record still gates and cross-checks the close
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/internal/creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts:96-99` requires `lineage.next === firstExpected + rows.length`; `:112-123` throws `CREATOR_ISSUANCE_RETIREMENT_UNAVAILABLE` for any row above the prior admitted boundary whose `decoded.epoch !== input.currentEpoch` or `decoded.anchor !== input.currentAnchorDigest`; `:124-127` throws when an in-graph row follows a truncated one. `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:936-949` runs `issuanceRetirementCandidate` unconditionally on every close and `:950-966` feeds its result in as `legacy`, which `:514-516` uses to seed the creator's own frontier. `packages/node/src/internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:325-331` requires exactly one retirement record in the proposed closure, and `:418-423` rejects the transition when the aggregate's creator frontier disagrees with the retirement record's `admittedAuthorSequence`. The design never mentions `drp-creator-issuance-retirement-state` and states only that "Creator-owned duplicate/regression errors keep their current fail-closed behavior".
findings.impact: A displaced or out-of-order row belonging to the creator's own issuance scope makes `deriveCreatorIssuanceRetirementBoundary` throw before any settlement logic runs, so the close aborts hard rather than settling — meaning the design's per-author `settledThrough` vector, which it says covers every successor ACL member, is unreachable for the creator itself. Even when the creator has no displaced rows, the design does not state the required relationship between the retirement record's `admittedAuthorSequence` and the checkpoint's creator `settledThrough`; the existing cross-check has no stated analogue, so a settlement-mode transition can be rejected or silently keep an admitted-not-settled creator boundary.
findings.required_action: State whether the creator's own author participates in settlement. If it does, name `internal/creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts` and `protocol-v3/src/creator-issuance-retirement.ts` as owners in a numbered slice and define the retirement↔checkpoint consistency rule that replaces `creator-transition-advance.ts:418-423`. If it does not, say so explicitly, state the exact fail-closed error the creator raises for its own displaced rows, and state how those rows are ever resolved — the design currently implies they are settleable while the source path aborts the close.

findings.title: Seeding the settled prefix from a v1 admitted prefix silently converts shipped reissue behavior into terminal drop
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4733-4790` — a local outbox row is `covered-historical` whenever `row.authorSequence <= identity.admittedAuthorSequence` and its epoch is below `closedEpoch`; the v1 frontier commits no per-sequence digest. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6445-6447` selects pending historical rows into the rebase outbox, and D.110c-0c1d (plan `docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:98746-98760`) fixed and now retains the behavior that such a pending row "is reissued and published once at the current epoch" on ordinary successor cold reopen. Design §"Recovery semantics and pruning" makes "any same-author issuance row at or below `settledThrough` … **terminal** … never republished, rebased, reduced or used as application evidence, regardless of its digest", and permits "a verified v1 frontier may seed the first settlement checkpoint". The crash/attack matrix has no row for a pending covered-historical row at the seeding boundary.
findings.impact: At the first opt-in close, every pending local row at or below the seeded prefix — including the honest offline peer's rows that D.110c-0c1d deliberately made survive by reissue — becomes terminal and is dropped, with no author settlement statement covering it and no operator-visible signal. The design asserts "unchanged v1 behavior without opt-in" but does not state this behavior change at opt-in, so an operator enabling `authorSettlementVersion: 1` silently loses queued honest operations. This is the one case where seeding is not justified by "effects are already in the authenticated snapshot": the admitted vertex's effects are, the local pending row's may not be.
findings.required_action: State the exact treatment of pending `covered-historical` rows at the seeding boundary — either a drain-and-settle barrier that must complete before the first opt-in close (owner f5b0c, with the room-side gate named), or explicit exclusion of still-pending slots from the seeded terminal range — and add the case to the crash/attack matrix with its required result.

findings.title: The reserved discriminator is not actually reserved against blueprint registration, and the recognition predicate is unstated for non-`action` discriminators
findings.evidence: `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:2708-2726` — `operationSchemaForPreparedAdmission` keys admission on `state.discriminator` and `state.operations`; nothing rejects a blueprint package that registers `$drp.author-settlement.v1`, and the discriminator key is blueprint-chosen rather than fixed to `action`. The design defines the control body as exactly `{ action, statement }` and calls the action "protocol-reserved" without stating enforcement.
findings.impact: An application blueprint could register the reserved action, letting an ordinary application operation be mistaken for a control body or a control body be routed into the reducer. A blueprint whose discriminator is not `action` leaves Node's recognition predicate undefined.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b0a. State that `prepareBlueprintAdmission` rejects any blueprint registering the reserved discriminator value, and state the exact predicate Node uses to recognize a control body (own data property `action` with the reserved value, independent of the blueprint discriminator). Disposition: fold into the f5b0a RED shape freeze; no recursive review required.

findings.title: The retirement-record fallback in openVerifiedCreatorHistoricalIssuance is not dispositioned for settlement mode
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:249-279` — with exactly one aggregate candidate the historical-issuance identity comes from the v1 frontier vector; with zero aggregate candidates it falls back to the retirement record and matches only when `opened.identity.author === input.author`, returning `undefined` for every other author. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4741-4747` makes `historicalIssuance === undefined` reject every historical row, and `:4349-4355` then reports "historical plane is at capacity".
findings.impact: In settlement mode there is no v1 aggregate, so unless this consumer is explicitly replaced the creator silently receives an admitted-not-settled boundary from the retirement record while every non-creator peer loses `covered-historical` classification entirely and `readRebaseOutbox()` fails.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b. State that in settlement mode `openVerifiedCreatorHistoricalIssuance` resolves from the settlement checkpoint for all authors and that the retirement fallback is disabled, and add the non-creator peer case to the matrix. Disposition: resolve while amending the design; it does not by itself change authority or executable scope.

findings.title: Baseline triggering and ordering are unowned, and an author that issues any ordinary vertex first is permanently stuck
findings.evidence: Design §"Exact carrier grammar" requires the baseline's `lineageNext` to equal its own outer author sequence and `retireThrough === lineageNext - 1`, and accepts it "during its first authorized epoch" only; design §"Creator checkpoint and advancement" accounts each slot by "exactly one graph vertex identity or exactly one same-author source disposition/baseline range". Design §"TDD implementation slices" gives f5b0c only "the opt-in, deterministic projection-presence query and internal result plumbing".
findings.impact: The baseline must be the author's first vertex of its first authorized epoch: if any ordinary vertex is issued first, the baseline's range double-accounts that slot and advancement stops, and the "first authorized epoch" restriction then prevents any later baseline — leaving that author permanently at a null boundary whose rows can never be settled or pruned. No component is assigned responsibility for triggering the baseline or guaranteeing the ordering.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b0c. Name the component that decides to author a baseline on join/re-entry and state the barrier that guarantees it precedes any ordinary issue in that epoch; alternatively relax "first authorized epoch" and permit `retireThrough < lineageNext - 1` so a later baseline remains possible. Disposition: resolve while amending the design; if the relaxation is chosen it changes the statement grammar and must land before f5b0a RED.

findings.title: Slice boundary is wrong for the protocol-v3 local-issue admission gate
findings.evidence: `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:3413-3415` — `createAdmissionBoundTransactionalVertexIssuer` rejects any operation for which `operationSchemaForPreparedAdmission` returns `undefined`, so the reserved control operation cannot be locally issued until protocol-v3 accepts it. The design assigns "the reserved admission path and `settleRebaseSources()`" to f5b0b (Node) while confining f5b0a GREEN to "protocol-v3 registry/codecs/exports and conformance".
findings.impact: With the slices as written, f5b0b's GREEN would have to modify protocol-v3, violating its own stated confinement, or f5b0b's RED cannot issue a real signed control vertex through the existing transactional path.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b0a. Extend f5b0a's stated GREEN scope to include the protocol-v3 issuer-side reserved-operation acceptance, or state explicitly that f5b0b may touch that one protocol-v3 function. Disposition: state the ownership in the amended design; no recursive review required.

findings.title: Cross-object migration-import displacement has no closed outcome in the settlement grammar
findings.evidence: `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2933-2946` — a displaced intent already satisfied by a migration import into a different target creator/object is skipped via `importedBytes` with no same-object replacement issued; `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6651-6680` shows cross-source completion marks the row published in the *source* object's store. The design's outcome grammar is closed to `already-present | expire | rebase | transform` (plus `settlement-control`), and requires every replacement to be "in the control vertex's current object, epoch and anchor".
findings.impact: A migration-import-satisfied intent is neither `already-present` in this object's snapshot base nor backed by a same-object replacement, so it has no representable disposition and its source can never be settled — leaving that author's boundary stuck on an otherwise-supported existing path.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b0c. Either state that migration/cross-object sources are out of settlement scope with the exact fail-closed behavior, or give the intent an explicit closed outcome (for example manual-review) and add it to the matrix. Disposition: resolve while amending the design; scoping it out does not change authority or the carrier grammar.

data.summary:
Scope of inspection: `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0-design-00a860ab/design.md` (complete), its `audit.md` and two-entry `manifest.sha256`, plan sections D.110c-0c1f5a / f5b0 / f5b (`docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:98036-98654`), and the named current source seams: `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts`, `creator-author-issuance-frontiers.ts`, `latched-acl.ts`, `registry/registry-v1.json`; `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts`, `v3-live.ts`, `internal/creator-transition-advance.ts`, `internal/creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts`, `internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts`; `packages/compaction/src/blueprint-fold.ts`; `packages/issuance-store/src/types.ts` and `maintenance.ts` with `packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts`; and `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts` around `drainRebaseOutbox()`/`issueOwned()` and the public application/session contracts. Honest limitation: this session has no shell, so I read the diff's product of `00a860ab..fc4b8fc7` (the frozen design, its audit, and the amended plan section) directly from the worktree and could not independently recompute the `a5dbd4f4…` manifest SHA-256 or the eight recorded source hashes; all findings below rest on directly read source, not on the audit's asserted digests.

Much of the construction is genuinely well matched to the current product. The transport choice is coherent: `registry/registry-v1.json` declares `kinds.vertex.fields.operation` as an unconstrained `canonical-object` signed under `ts-drp/vertex/v3`, and pins `authorSequence.constraints.reset = "never"`, which the design preserves — so a reserved operation inside the ordinary signed vertex needs no wire field, no second signature, no new suite and no dependency. The old/downgraded-peer barrier really does fail closed: `internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:398` requires exactly one `drp-creator-author-issuance-frontiers-state` in the proposed closure, so an old binary rejects a settlement-mode successor with `TRUST_CLOSURE_INVALID` rather than continuing. The ≤64 frontier vector fits: `latched-acl.ts:134` caps ACL members at 64 and `:148` already enforces strict code-unit author ordering, so "every successor ACL member, not only writers" is representable within the existing `copiedFrontiers` bound. `historyRoot`/`historySize` are available before the checkpoint is prepared (`creator-close.ts:874-882` precedes `:950`), so binding them is implementable. `V3LocalIssueResult` (`v3-live.ts:506`) already carries `{authorSequence, digest}`, and `V3RoomApplication` / `CreateV3RoomSessionInput` (`examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:351,377`) accommodate `hasDisplacedOperation` and `authorSettlementVersion?: 1` as a minimal public boundary. f5a's per-author close-liveness result is not reopened.

The construction nevertheless cannot be authorized as written. Two defects are P0. First, the central admission rule — "enters the causality index, close set, history … but never blueprint admission/reduction" — is unimplementable from the named seams and aborts every close either way: `captureCloseGraph()` (`v3-live.ts:7430-7457`) hard-requires `applicationVertices.size === applicationAuthors.size + 1 === applicationCharges.size + 1 === index.size`, the close set and RFC 9162 history are derived from exactly that map (`creator-close.ts:874-882`), and the same map is handed to `foldBlueprintEpoch` (`v3-live.ts:7039-7051`), which applies **every** vertex through `applyPreparedBlueprintOperation` with no skip and demands `authorize(...) === true` under write authorization (`packages/compaction/src/blueprint-fold.ts:208-228`). Excluding the control vertex breaks the capture invariant and removes the very graph slot the checkpoint scan depends on; including it makes the reducer reject the reserved action. `@ts-drp/compaction` is named in none of the four slices. Second, the author-baseline does not preserve never-resetting issuance: because a fully removed key is *omitted* from the vector, the creator retains no authenticated prior boundary for it, and the baseline is accepted for any author "absent from the prior authenticated checkpoint" with `retireThrough === null` when `lineageNext === 0` — so a removed-and-readmitted same key can restart at sequence 0 and obtain a fresh creator-certified `settledThrough` over slots already signed under different digests. That is precisely the compact unproved maximum (and reset) the design says it prohibits, and the enforcement it relies on lives only in the settling author's own store.

Five further P1s follow the same pattern of promised outcomes without a named owner: settled rows cannot actually leave custody (`closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:404-428` and `browser-issuance-store.ts:651-658` both refuse any prefix whose rows are not all `epoch === closedEpoch` and `published`, so one surviving old-epoch displaced row freezes the watermark forever, and once unpruned covered rows exceed `maxEpochVertices` the room hard-fails at `v3-live.ts:4419`); every vertex-authentication path threads `preparedBlueprintAdmission` (six Node call sites), so the first control row that survives into a later outbox makes `readRebaseOutbox()` return `record-rejected` and the room throw; `ReplacementRef` carries no batch entry index while the room routinely batches up to 16 replacements into one vertex (`examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2654-2681`), so the creator cannot verify the "exact ordered replacement identities" the statement claims to bind; the creator's own author cannot be settled at all because `deriveCreatorIssuanceRetirementBoundary` hard-throws on exactly the displaced-row shape (`creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts:112-127`) and the unmentioned `drp-creator-issuance-retirement-state` record is still cross-checked against the frontier (`creator-transition-advance.ts:418-423`); and seeding the settled prefix from a v1 admitted prefix silently converts today's shipped D.110c-0c1d behavior — pending `covered-historical` rows are reissued at the current epoch — into terminal drop, without an author statement and without a matrix row.

Because at least P0-2 (baseline statement/vector shape) and P1-5 (`ReplacementRef` grammar) change the exact canonical shapes f5b0a RED is meant to freeze, and P0-1/P1-4 change what "the reserved carrier is accepted as" across protocol-v3 and Node, the f5b0a protocol-codec/compatibility RED may not begin as sliced. Amend the design per the required actions, then re-review. Do not implement a nearby substitute. Nothing here authorizes production GREEN or a retained campaign, and f5a's foreign-anomaly result is untouched.

findings.title: Reserved control vertex cannot be in the close graph without entering the blueprint reducer; either branch aborts every close
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:7430-7457` — `captureCloseGraph()` returns `undefined` unless `applicationVertices.size === applicationAuthors.size + 1 === applicationCharges.size + 1 === registration.index.size`. `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:874-882` derives the close-set root, history root and history size from exactly `graph.vertices` / `graph.charges` / `graph.frontier`, and `:487-498` builds the per-author slot map from `graph.authors`. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:7039-7051` hands `copyApplicationVertices(registration.applicationVertices)` to `foldBlueprintEpoch` with `authorize` = `isV3ApplicationAuthorAuthorized` (`:3449-3455`, i.e. `authorizeLatchedApplicationWrite`, permissionless-or-writer). `packages/compaction/src/blueprint-fold.ts:208-228` iterates every vertex in that map, filtering only the anchor hash, throws `BLUEPRINT_AUTHORIZATION_REJECTED` unless `authorize(...) === true`, and calls `stagedMachine.apply(vertex.operation)` → `applyPreparedBlueprintOperation`, which raises `BLUEPRINT_OPERATION_INVALID` for an unregistered action. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3956-3961` shows `retainApplicationVertex` is called immediately after `index.append`, so the two maps are populated together today. Design §"Admission and durable lifecycle" requires both "appends the vertex to the ordinary causality index" / "appears in the close set and RFC 9162 history" and "does not call blueprint operation admission … reducer", and design §"TDD implementation slices" names only protocol-v3, Node, the room and the creator — `@ts-drp/compaction` is named in no slice.
findings.impact: Neither branch is viable. If the control vertex is appended to the causality index but not retained in `applicationVertices`, `captureCloseGraph()` returns `undefined` and `creator-close.ts:847` throws `creator close graph capture failed`, aborting the close; the vertex is also absent from the close set, the history commitment and `graph.authors`, so the design's own rule that "a control vertex's own author sequence is an ordinary graph slot" is false and the checkpoint scan cannot account it. If it is retained, `foldBlueprintEpoch` reduces it, `stageBlueprintEpoch()` returns `fold-rejected`, `stageSnapshot()` fails and `creator-close.ts:841` throws `creator snapshot export failed: not-active` — again aborting the whole close. Separately, the design gates admission on "current ACL envelope membership" (`authorizeLatchedEnvelopeAuthor`, membership only) while the fold predicate requires write authorization, so a member holding only `admin` or `finality` could author one control vertex and permanently abort every close in the room — a room-wide liveness loss from a single authorized non-writer.
findings.required_action: Amend the design to name `@ts-drp/compaction` (`foldBlueprintEpoch`) and `v3-live.ts`'s `captureCloseGraph` / `retainApplicationVertex` accounting as explicit owners, and state the exact rule that excludes reserved control operations from reduction while retaining graph, charge, frontier, close-set and history membership — including the revised capture invariants. State the exact admission authority for the control body (envelope membership vs. application write authorization) and make the fold predicate and the admission predicate provably consistent, so no authorized member can abort a close. Assign the compaction owner to a numbered slice (extend f5b0b or open a new one); it is currently unowned.

findings.title: Author-baseline permits same-key sequence reset after ACL removal, becoming the compact unproved maximum the design forbids
findings.evidence: Design §"Exact carrier grammar": a baseline is "accepted only for an author absent from the prior authenticated checkpoint, during its first authorized epoch, when the outer control vertex author sequence equals `lineageNext`, and only when `retireThrough === null` iff `lineageNext === 0`". Design §"Creator checkpoint and advancement": "A fully removed key is omitted and may return only through the author-baseline rule above." `packages/protocol-v3/src/latched-acl.ts:3` — `AUTHOR = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/`, i.e. the ACL author *is* the raw Ed25519 public key, so "a fresh author key" means a different ACL member. `packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-author-issuance-frontiers.ts:164-185` bounds the vector at 64 entries; `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:511` iterates only `successorAuthors`, so an omitted author's boundary is unrecoverable from the checkpoint chain. The only stated enforcement is prose: "Same-key membership re-entry therefore requires the original monotonic issuance store; loss of that store fails closed and requires a fresh author key."
findings.impact: An author whose durable issuance store is lost (or who chooses to) can be removed from the ACL and re-added by any admin, then issue a baseline with `lineageNext = 0` and `retireThrough = null`. The creator's stated checks — absence from the prior checkpoint, outer sequence equals `lineageNext`, `retireThrough` arithmetic — all pass, and it certifies a fresh `settledThrough` over sequences `0..k` that already exist under different vertex digests in earlier signed checkpoints and archived history. This is exactly the sequence reset/reuse the registry pins as `reset: "never"` and the design says it prohibits, and it is precisely a compact unproved maximum. It also defeats the design's claim that "exact source uniqueness prevents replay, substitution, equivocation": that uniqueness is scoped to a single close graph, so cross-checkpoint slot reuse is never detected. There is no creator-side fact that distinguishes an honest preserved-lineage baseline from a fabricated one.
findings.required_action: Choose and state one enforceable rule: (a) retain removed members' boundaries as authenticated tombstones in the checkpoint and reconcile the resulting growth with the ≤64 vector bound explicitly; or (b) require the baseline to name the exact prior authenticated checkpoint digest and that author's boundary in it, and have the creator verify `lineageNext > priorSettledThrough` against an authenticated predecessor chain; or (c) restrict baselines to authors that have never appeared in any authenticated predecessor checkpoint, and state the exact fail-closed behavior for a returning key. Whichever is chosen changes the baseline statement shape and/or the checkpoint vector, so it must be settled before f5b0a RED freezes canonical shapes.

findings.title: Settled rows cannot leave active custody; state grows with epoch count and hard-fails the rebase outbox reader
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:404-428` — `copiedIssuance` requires a dense prefix beginning at `prunedThroughAuthorSequence + 1`, with every row satisfying `Number(candidate.epoch) === closedEpoch`, `issued === true`, `outbox === true` and `publishState === "published"`; any deviation returns `D109A_OUTBOX_INCOMPLETE`. `packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts:651-658` — `prunePublishedPrefix` throws `invalid("selected issuance row belongs to another epoch")` when `decoded.epoch !== captured.closedEpoch` and `ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED` when any row is still `pending`. `packages/issuance-store/src/types.ts:83-90` — `DurableIssuanceStore` exposes no delete; pruning is the only reclamation. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4349-4355` and `:6418-6425` — `countHistoricalIssuanceRow` caps historical rows at `maxEpochVertices` and `readRebaseOutbox` returns `record-rejected` ("v3 rebase historical plane is at capacity") past that bound; `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2801` turns that into a thrown room failure. Design §"Recovery semantics and pruning" asserts "Existing closed-epoch cleanup may prune them only after durable checkpoint staging, verified successor adoption, rollback-generation retention and availability conditions" and "No state grows with epoch count or number of completed rebases"; neither `closed-epoch-cleanup.ts` nor the issuance-store pruning contract (which has a conformance suite at `packages/issuance-store/src/conformance.ts`) is named as an owner in any slice.
findings.impact: A displaced source row from epoch k that survives above the prune watermark — the exact state settlement exists to create — makes every later single-epoch cleanup refuse with `D109A_OUTBOX_INCOMPLETE`, so the watermark freezes permanently and the outbox grows with every subsequently issued row, i.e. with epoch count. This is not a soft bound: once the unpruned rows at or below the covered/settled boundary exceed `maxEpochVertices`, `readRebaseOutbox()` fails and the room session becomes terminal. The design's age-independence claim is therefore both unmet and load-bearing, and the mechanism that would reclaim the rows refuses the mixed-epoch prefix by construction.
findings.required_action: Name `packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts` and the `@ts-drp/issuance-store` pruning contract with its browser implementation as explicit owners in a numbered slice. State the exact prune rule for a settled prefix that spans epochs — whether `prunePublishedPrefix`'s single-`closedEpoch` and published-only preconditions change, whether multiple per-epoch calls are used, and whether this is a durable-store contract and conformance-vector change (the plan's f5b0 obligation 10 requires this to be frozen, not deferred). If settled old-epoch rows are instead retained, state the exact bound and reconcile it with the `maxEpochVertices` historical cap that hard-fails `readRebaseOutbox()`.

findings.title: Every recovery, rebase and local-issue authentication path rejects a control vertex; the design names only Node ingress
findings.evidence: `preparedBlueprintAdmission` is threaded through six Node authentication sites — `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:2019`, `:2336`, `:3806` (ingress via `extractAuthorizedV3Vertex`), `:4699` (pinned-genesis outbox row), `:4770` (`authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow`, lines 4733-4790) and `:5977` — plus the local issuer gate in `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:3413-3415`, where `operationSchemaForPreparedAdmission` (`:2708-2726`) returns `undefined` for any discriminator absent from the blueprint's registered operations. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6400-6416` turns an unclassifiable outbox row into `record-rejected` ("v3 rebase outbox record is invalid"), and `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2800-2805` throws on that result. Design §"Admission and durable lifecycle" describes only "Node admission authenticates the normal vertex first … then appends the vertex to the ordinary causality index", and design §"TDD implementation slices" assigns "the reserved admission path" solely to f5b0b while confining f5b0a GREEN to "protocol-v3 registry/codecs/exports and conformance".
findings.impact: The first settlement control vertex that survives into a later epoch's issuance outbox cannot be classified by `classifyRebaseRow`/`authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow`, so `readRebaseOutbox()` returns `record-rejected` and the room throws `v3 room rebase outbox failed: record-rejected`, making the session terminal. The design's own rule that "an older settlement-control row is never handed to the application" and is "covered by a later `settlement-control` source entry" therefore has no reachable implementation, and the crash-matrix row "control journaled but unpublished → restart republishes it" is not satisfiable. Local issue of the control vertex is likewise rejected by protocol-v3 before Node is reached.
findings.required_action: Enumerate in the design every `preparedBlueprintAdmission` call site that must recognize the reserved action — ingress, pinned-genesis and covered-historical outbox classification, displaced/recovery authentication, and the protocol-v3 admission-bound transactional issuer — and assign each to a named slice with its exact accept/skip rule. State explicitly how `rebaseIntents` treats a control row and how a terminal (at/below prefix) control row is skipped without failing the scan.

findings.title: ReplacementRef cannot identify a replacement operation inside a batched vertex, so the creator cannot verify the exact ordered replacements the statement claims to bind
findings.evidence: Design §"Exact carrier grammar": `ReplacementRef = { operationDigest; vertex: [epoch, anchorDigest, authorSequence, vertexDigest] }` — no operation index — while the source side does carry `operationIndex` and `operationCount` in `IntentDisposition`. The design gives one formula, `operationDigest = hashDomain("ts-drp/author-settlement-operation/v1", encodeCanonical(operation))`, without saying whether `operation` is the individual application operation or the vertex's whole operation, and requires the creator to verify each ref against "its canonical inner operation digest". `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2654-2681` — `drainSnapshot` groups up to 16 batchable operations of the same `group` into a single `issueOwned` → `issueLocal` call, and `:2950-2962` shows rebase/transform replacements are pushed onto exactly that `pendingIssues` path with `group = action\0policy`. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5844-5865` confirms the resulting vertex carries the single `applicationBatch` action wrapping `batch.entries`.
findings.impact: On the room's normal replacement path a single vertex carries several distinct replacement operations. If `operationDigest` is taken over the vertex operation it is one value shared by up to 16 entries and identifies nothing; if it is taken over an individual entry the creator cannot locate that entry, since the ref carries no index. Either way the creator's verification collapses to "some same-author ancestor vertex with this digest exists", and the design's central claim that the signed statement "binds … exact ordered current replacements" — the basis for its substitution and reordering resistance in review question 2 — is not delivered by the grammar.
findings.required_action: Either add an explicit batch entry index (and the containing operation count) to `ReplacementRef` and state the exact digest preimage for each, or forbid batching for replacement issues and state the room-side rule that guarantees one replacement operation per vertex. State which, and disambiguate the single `operationDigest` formula into the source-intent case and the replacement case. This changes a canonical shape f5b0a RED is meant to freeze.

findings.title: The creator's own author cannot be settled, and the unmentioned creator-issuance-retirement record still gates and cross-checks the close
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/internal/creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts:96-99` requires `lineage.next === firstExpected + rows.length`; `:112-123` throws `CREATOR_ISSUANCE_RETIREMENT_UNAVAILABLE` for any row above the prior admitted boundary whose `decoded.epoch !== input.currentEpoch` or `decoded.anchor !== input.currentAnchorDigest`; `:124-127` throws when an in-graph row follows a truncated one. `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:936-949` runs `issuanceRetirementCandidate` unconditionally on every close and `:950-966` feeds its result in as `legacy`, which `:514-516` uses to seed the creator's own frontier. `packages/node/src/internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:325-331` requires exactly one retirement record in the proposed closure, and `:418-423` rejects the transition when the aggregate's creator frontier disagrees with the retirement record's `admittedAuthorSequence`. The design never mentions `drp-creator-issuance-retirement-state` and states only that "Creator-owned duplicate/regression errors keep their current fail-closed behavior".
findings.impact: A displaced or out-of-order row belonging to the creator's own issuance scope makes `deriveCreatorIssuanceRetirementBoundary` throw before any settlement logic runs, so the close aborts hard rather than settling — meaning the design's per-author `settledThrough` vector, which it says covers every successor ACL member, is unreachable for the creator itself. Even when the creator has no displaced rows, the design does not state the required relationship between the retirement record's `admittedAuthorSequence` and the checkpoint's creator `settledThrough`; the existing cross-check has no stated analogue, so a settlement-mode transition can be rejected or silently keep an admitted-not-settled creator boundary.
findings.required_action: State whether the creator's own author participates in settlement. If it does, name `internal/creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts` and `protocol-v3/src/creator-issuance-retirement.ts` as owners in a numbered slice and define the retirement↔checkpoint consistency rule that replaces `creator-transition-advance.ts:418-423`. If it does not, say so explicitly, state the exact fail-closed error the creator raises for its own displaced rows, and state how those rows are ever resolved — the design currently implies they are settleable while the source path aborts the close.

findings.title: Seeding the settled prefix from a v1 admitted prefix silently converts shipped reissue behavior into terminal drop
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4733-4790` — a local outbox row is `covered-historical` whenever `row.authorSequence <= identity.admittedAuthorSequence` and its epoch is below `closedEpoch`; the v1 frontier commits no per-sequence digest. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6445-6447` selects pending historical rows into the rebase outbox, and D.110c-0c1d (plan `docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:98746-98760`) fixed and now retains the behavior that such a pending row "is reissued and published once at the current epoch" on ordinary successor cold reopen. Design §"Recovery semantics and pruning" makes "any same-author issuance row at or below `settledThrough` … **terminal** … never republished, rebased, reduced or used as application evidence, regardless of its digest", and permits "a verified v1 frontier may seed the first settlement checkpoint". The crash/attack matrix has no row for a pending covered-historical row at the seeding boundary.
findings.impact: At the first opt-in close, every pending local row at or below the seeded prefix — including the honest offline peer's rows that D.110c-0c1d deliberately made survive by reissue — becomes terminal and is dropped, with no author settlement statement covering it and no operator-visible signal. The design asserts "unchanged v1 behavior without opt-in" but does not state this behavior change at opt-in, so an operator enabling `authorSettlementVersion: 1` silently loses queued honest operations. This is the one case where seeding is not justified by "effects are already in the authenticated snapshot": the admitted vertex's effects are, the local pending row's may not be.
findings.required_action: State the exact treatment of pending `covered-historical` rows at the seeding boundary — either a drain-and-settle barrier that must complete before the first opt-in close (owner f5b0c, with the room-side gate named), or explicit exclusion of still-pending slots from the seeded terminal range — and add the case to the crash/attack matrix with its required result.

findings.title: The reserved discriminator is not actually reserved against blueprint registration, and the recognition predicate is unstated for non-`action` discriminators
findings.evidence: `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:2708-2726` — `operationSchemaForPreparedAdmission` keys admission on `state.discriminator` and `state.operations`; nothing rejects a blueprint package that registers `$drp.author-settlement.v1`, and the discriminator key is blueprint-chosen rather than fixed to `action`. The design defines the control body as exactly `{ action, statement }` and calls the action "protocol-reserved" without stating enforcement.
findings.impact: An application blueprint could register the reserved action, letting an ordinary application operation be mistaken for a control body or a control body be routed into the reducer. A blueprint whose discriminator is not `action` leaves Node's recognition predicate undefined.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b0a. State that `prepareBlueprintAdmission` rejects any blueprint registering the reserved discriminator value, and state the exact predicate Node uses to recognize a control body (own data property `action` with the reserved value, independent of the blueprint discriminator). Disposition: fold into the f5b0a RED shape freeze; no recursive review required.

findings.title: The retirement-record fallback in openVerifiedCreatorHistoricalIssuance is not dispositioned for settlement mode
findings.evidence: `packages/node/src/internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:249-279` — with exactly one aggregate candidate the historical-issuance identity comes from the v1 frontier vector; with zero aggregate candidates it falls back to the retirement record and matches only when `opened.identity.author === input.author`, returning `undefined` for every other author. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4741-4747` makes `historicalIssuance === undefined` reject every historical row, and `:4349-4355` then reports "historical plane is at capacity".
findings.impact: In settlement mode there is no v1 aggregate, so unless this consumer is explicitly replaced the creator silently receives an admitted-not-settled boundary from the retirement record while every non-creator peer loses `covered-historical` classification entirely and `readRebaseOutbox()` fails.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b. State that in settlement mode `openVerifiedCreatorHistoricalIssuance` resolves from the settlement checkpoint for all authors and that the retirement fallback is disabled, and add the non-creator peer case to the matrix. Disposition: resolve while amending the design; it does not by itself change authority or executable scope.

findings.title: Baseline triggering and ordering are unowned, and an author that issues any ordinary vertex first is permanently stuck
findings.evidence: Design §"Exact carrier grammar" requires the baseline's `lineageNext` to equal its own outer author sequence and `retireThrough === lineageNext - 1`, and accepts it "during its first authorized epoch" only; design §"Creator checkpoint and advancement" accounts each slot by "exactly one graph vertex identity or exactly one same-author source disposition/baseline range". Design §"TDD implementation slices" gives f5b0c only "the opt-in, deterministic projection-presence query and internal result plumbing".
findings.impact: The baseline must be the author's first vertex of its first authorized epoch: if any ordinary vertex is issued first, the baseline's range double-accounts that slot and advancement stops, and the "first authorized epoch" restriction then prevents any later baseline — leaving that author permanently at a null boundary whose rows can never be settled or pruned. No component is assigned responsibility for triggering the baseline or guaranteeing the ordering.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b0c. Name the component that decides to author a baseline on join/re-entry and state the barrier that guarantees it precedes any ordinary issue in that epoch; alternatively relax "first authorized epoch" and permit `retireThrough < lineageNext - 1` so a later baseline remains possible. Disposition: resolve while amending the design; if the relaxation is chosen it changes the statement grammar and must land before f5b0a RED.

findings.title: Slice boundary is wrong for the protocol-v3 local-issue admission gate
findings.evidence: `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:3413-3415` — `createAdmissionBoundTransactionalVertexIssuer` rejects any operation for which `operationSchemaForPreparedAdmission` returns `undefined`, so the reserved control operation cannot be locally issued until protocol-v3 accepts it. The design assigns "the reserved admission path and `settleRebaseSources()`" to f5b0b (Node) while confining f5b0a GREEN to "protocol-v3 registry/codecs/exports and conformance".
findings.impact: With the slices as written, f5b0b's GREEN would have to modify protocol-v3, violating its own stated confinement, or f5b0b's RED cannot issue a real signed control vertex through the existing transactional path.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b0a. Extend f5b0a's stated GREEN scope to include the protocol-v3 issuer-side reserved-operation acceptance, or state explicitly that f5b0b may touch that one protocol-v3 function. Disposition: state the ownership in the amended design; no recursive review required.

findings.title: Cross-object migration-import displacement has no closed outcome in the settlement grammar
findings.evidence: `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2933-2946` — a displaced intent already satisfied by a migration import into a different target creator/object is skipped via `importedBytes` with no same-object replacement issued; `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6651-6680` shows cross-source completion marks the row published in the *source* object's store. The design's outcome grammar is closed to `already-present | expire | rebase | transform` (plus `settlement-control`), and requires every replacement to be "in the control vertex's current object, epoch and anchor".
findings.impact: A migration-import-satisfied intent is neither `already-present` in this object's snapshot base nor backed by a same-object replacement, so it has no representable disposition and its source can never be settled — leaving that author's boundary stuck on an otherwise-supported existing path.
findings.required_action: Owner f5b0c. Either state that migration/cross-object sources are out of settlement scope with the exact fail-closed behavior, or give the intent an explicit closed outcome (for example manual-review) and add it to the matrix. Disposition: resolve while amending the design; scoping it out does not change authority or the carrier grammar.
